findings.issue: DRIFT: T186 says `--calibrate` prints the table and exits 0; runTriage writes it at :892 and main() writes the returned table again at :1047 (`if (args.calibrate || !args.jsonOnly)`), so the CLI prints the calibration table twice (probe in a copied root: "calibration table header printed 2 time(s)"; the unit test calls runTriage directly and never sees it)
findings.fix: drop the `args.calibrate ||` clause or the write at :892

findings.issue: DRIFT: design wires review-triage.ts → decide.ts, but the map has no `s_review_triage --imports--> l_decide` or `s_decide_test --imports--> l_decide` edge; `TS_IMPORT_RE` (scripts/lib/system-map-lib.ts:330) is line-anchored and both files use multi-line `import { ... } from "./lib/decide.ts"` (review-triage.ts:21-34), so `l_decide` shows "1 dependent" and the sole consumer is invisible
findings.fix: extend extractTsImports to join multi-line import statements (pre-existing extractor gap, surfaced by this feature)

findings.issue: DRIFT: T185 says a partial rejection sets `declined: "malformed-response"`; the result does, but the `jev-queried` kv has no `declined`/`reason` key, so the audit log cannot distinguish a clean from a partially-rejected response (the T185 completion-report deviation describes only the event name)
findings.fix: add `declined: "malformed-response"` to the jev-queried kv when anyRejected

findings.issue: DRIFT: design's review-triage.json header carries `declined`; with zero findings no chunk is built, decide() is never called, and the header omits `declined` entirely (probe: `{"backend":"heuristic","findings":0}`); with multiple chunks only `results[0].declined` is reported
findings.fix: call decide once on an empty question map or derive `declined` from all results

findings.issue: DRIFT: T184 says `file:lines` splits at the last `:` with `lines=""` only when there is no `:`; splitFileLines also keeps the whole token as `file` when the suffix is not `N`/`N-M` (Windows `C:/x` safe, but a `foo.ts:abc` line silently becomes file `foo.ts:abc`)
findings.fix: accept as a refinement or document it in the docstring

findings.issue: DRIFT: design says applyAnswers "replaces a heuristic value with the Jev value only above the matching threshold"; a non-`unrelated` scope choice is applied with no threshold (fixture: architecture-2 heuristic `unrelated` → Jev `in_diff`), which is a defensible reading of `out_of_scope_p` but is the source of `scope_changed: 1` in the lift record
findings.fix: confirm intent; if in_diff/adjacent should also be gated, gate on `probabilities[choice] >= out_of_scope_p`

findings.issue: DRIFT: T186 says header `redactions` = the output guard's count; on refusal every field counts as a redaction (`outputRedactions = outboundFields.length`) and decide's per-chunk redactions are summed in too, so the number mixes wire and local counts
findings.fix: document or split into `redactions` and `withheld`

findings.issue: DRIFT: T183 specifies `execFileSync("node", [...])`; implementation uses `process.execPath` (more robust, but not the brief's shape)
findings.fix: accept; note in the completion report

findings.issue: DRIFT: T179 signature is `defaultLogger(event, kv)`; a third `cwd?` parameter was added for the T179 test
findings.fix: accept (test-driven, harmless)

findings.issue: DRIFT: design cites `scan-rules.js:1620`, `:824`, `:2551` and tasks.md `:2546-2565`; the prettier reformat moved every rule (file 2570 → 3021 lines; bare-sk-token now at :2995), so those anchors are stale
findings.fix: none required for code; a note in the ADR would help

findings.issue: VULN: denylist redaction misses `KEY="value"` (quote excluded from value class), `key = value` (whitespace around `=`), and `key: value` (colon) shapes; probe: `TOKEN="abc123def456"`, `api_key = '...'`, `privateKey: abcdefghij1234567890` each returned 0 redactions, so low-entropy secrets in the commonest finding-prose shapes reach the wire
findings.fix: allow optional whitespace, a `:` separator, and quoted values in both regexes

findings.issue: VULN: entropy floor 4.0 bits/char is unreachable for hex-charset tokens (max log2(16)=4.0); probe through the real guard: 32/40/64-char hex keys scored 3.64/3.90/3.67 and passed scrub, re-scan, denylist and entropy (`hex leaks: true`)
findings.fix: use a length/charset-aware bar (as scanner's effectiveEntropyThreshold) or add a `[0-9a-f]{32,}` redaction

findings.issue: VULN: a staged field containing the scanner's inline marker `scan-allow` is skipped by BOTH scrub and the positive re-scan, so "verified clean" is vacuous for that line and only the entropy floor remains; probe: ghp_ token on a `scan-allow` line came back `[REDACTED:entropy]` not `[REDACTED:github-pat]`; a hex/low-entropy secret on such a line leaks; reviewer reports in this repo plausibly quote `scan-allow`
findings.fix: neutralize the marker in fields before staging, or run the subprocess with `--allowlist` pointing at a file whose `inline.marker` cannot occur

findings.issue: VULN: literal GitHub-PAT-shaped token (exact 36-char class) committed; invisible to the scanner only because `tests/fixtures/**` is path-ignored (allowlist.json:10)
findings.fix: obviously fake; optionally build it at test time by concatenation

findings.issue: VULN: local review-triage.json and stdout table guard only `issue`/`fix`; `file`, `lines`, `id` are written unscrubbed though the design says every text field is the scrubbed value
findings.fix: add `file` to outboundFields

findings.issue: VULN: `config.model` (settings-controlled string) is serialized into the body without passing the guard; a settings edit can carry arbitrary text to the vendor
findings.fix: validate `model` against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$` in readJevConfig

findings.issue: VULN: `probabilities` values only checked finite, not [0,1], and score `probabilities` accepts unbounded keys; a value >1 satisfies review-triage.ts:504 and is written as `in_scope_p`
findings.fix: require isUnitInterval per probability; require score keys within 0..n-1

findings.issue: VULN: `Bash(node scripts/review-triage.ts*)` auto-approves any argv; `<spec-dir>`, `--changed-files`, `--calibrate` paths are unconstrained (review-triage.ts:801,812,818,887,965), so an auto-approved command can read any file (its lines go outbound via the guard when Jev is on) and drop review-triage.json into any writable dir
findings.fix: accept as consistent with sibling entries, or constrain paths under docs/specs in main()

findings.issue: VULN: TOCTOU — realpath containment checked on the directory, file created later with `wx`; swapping `.claude/logs/jev` for a symlink in between lands the staging file outside root (same-user attacker only)
findings.fix: re-verify realpath of the created file before scrub

findings.issue: VULN: mode 0o700 applies only when the dir is created; a pre-existing wider-mode `jev/` is never tightened
findings.fix: chmodSync(real, 0o700) after mkdir

findings.issue: VULN: scanner subprocess has no `timeout`; a hung scanner hangs the triage run (availability only; fail-closed)
findings.fix: pass `timeout` to execFileSync

findings.issue: VULN: `response.json()` has no size bound and is limited only by `AbortSignal.timeout`, while readJevConfig accepts any finite non-negative timeout_ms (e.g. 1e12)
findings.fix: cap timeout_ms and read the body with a byte cap

findings.issue: VULN: `--calibrate` extra paths read without existsSync; ENOENT stack trace exposes only the path
findings.fix: existsSync + warn

findings.issue: ISSUE: `applyAnswers` merges every result's answers once any chunk has `backend==="jev"`; a chunk that declined (timeout/network) or a question rejected as malformed carries heuristic stubs (noul 0.5, choice "in_diff") that clear the consumer's heuristic pairing (0.5 < 0.85 → `duplicate_of=null`) and flip scope to `in_diff` unconditionally; `declined` is never consulted
findings.fix: skip results with `backend==="heuristic"` and answers whose name-level validation failed (expose rejected names on `DecisionResult`), then add test: setup two chunks, one result declined "timeout" + one jev; action applyAnswers; assert declined chunk's rows keep heuristic `duplicate_of`/`in_scope`

findings.issue: ISSUE: `runTriage` writes the calibration table to stdout itself, then `main()` writes the returned `table` again → `--calibrate` from the CLI prints everything twice; also spams test output (visible in the run above)
findings.fix: drop the write at :892 and let `main()` own stdout; add CLI test: setup fixture, action run with `--calibrate`, assert stdout contains the header exactly once

findings.issue: ISSUE: `runTriage` is 190 lines mixing report loading, decide fan-out, calibration, output scrubbing, logging, and file writes
findings.fix: extract `loadFindings()`, `runCalibration()`, `scrubOutputRows()`

findings.issue: ISSUE: `decide()` is 172 lines
findings.fix: extract `postToJev()` (fetch + status→reason mapping) and `validateResponse()` (doc→answers/usage)

findings.issue: ISSUE: `computeAgreement` re-implements the three threshold rules of `applyAnswers` by hand; the two can drift silently
findings.fix: extract `thresholdedDup/Scope/Severity(answer, thresholds)` helpers and call them from both

findings.issue: ISSUE: `decide()` hardcodes `getProjectRoot()` for the guard so Jev-path tests stage under the real repo's `.claude/logs/jev-test-*` and create a symlink in the real `.claude/logs`, contrary to the design ("no test touches this repo's `.claude/logs/`") and the Copied-Project-Root pattern
findings.fix: add `projectRoot?` to `DecideDeps` (runTriage already takes one) and stage in a temp root

findings.issue: ISSUE: no threshold-boundary tests: noul exactly 0.85, `probabilities.unrelated` exactly 0.8, confidence exactly 0.8 (all `>=` inclusive); no test that `unrelated` below threshold keeps the heuristic scope, nor that `in_scope_p` is set
findings.fix: add setup single finding, action applyAnswers with the exact boundary value, assert merged/applied

findings.issue: ISSUE: `scoreToLevel` half-rounding tested only at 1.5; 0.5→LOW, 2.5→HIGH, 3.0→CRITICAL, and clamping of <0 / >3 untested
findings.fix: parametrize over those scores and assert the level

findings.issue: ISSUE: design-named cases missing: `decide_scrubSubprocessNonZero_declinesScrubFailed` (impl at egress-guard.ts:302-308 ignores a nonzero scrub status — either the design or the guard is wrong; pin one), non-JSON body, `answers` absent, a question missing from `answers` (count mismatch), all answers rejected → `declined:"malformed-response"` with `backend:"heuristic"`, `readJevConfig` file-present-but-no-jev-block and unparseable JSON
findings.fix: one test each: setup stub response, action decide, assert `declined`/`backend`/answer deep-equals heuristic

findings.issue: ISSUE: no zero-findings run (empty/missing review-raw → `chunks=[]`, `results=[]`, `declined=undefined`) and no missing-`extraReviews`-file case (`readFileSync` at review-triage.ts:812 throws uncaught, CLI dies with a stack trace)
findings.fix: add setup empty spec dir, action runTriage, assert `findings:[]`, `declined===undefined`; add setup bogus calibrate path, assert a usage-style error not a throw

findings.issue: ISSUE: Jaccard pairing tested only below threshold; the `>= 0.6` branch (review-triage.ts:227) and its exact boundary are never exercised
findings.fix: add setup two findings in different files with 3-of-5 shared tokens, action heuristicCandidates, assert pair emitted

findings.issue: ISSUE: magic `0.6` Jaccard threshold, hardcoded `3` in `scoreToLevel`, and `["LOW","MEDIUM","HIGH","CRITICAL"]` literal duplicated before `SEVERITY_LEVELS` is declared
findings.fix: `const JACCARD_DUP_THRESHOLD = 0.6`; `SEVERITY_LEVELS.length - 1`; reuse `SEVERITY_LEVELS` in `severityQuestion`

findings.issue: ISSUE: `/ 4` chars-per-token estimate and the 24/4.0 entropy floor are unnamed; `egress-allowlist.json` records `entropy>=4.0` with no test tying it to the code
findings.fix: `CHARS_PER_TOKEN`, exported `ENTROPY_MIN_LEN`/`ENTROPY_MIN_BITS`, and extend `egressAllowlist_*` to assert the guard string

findings.issue: ISSUE: question-map construction for a finding is duplicated in the "extend current chunk" and "new chunk" branches of `buildQuestions` (67 lines)
